- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.67) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.33) — model fails to recognize bearish momentum, leading to lagged corrections.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in trending upticks and too low in downtrends — adjust forecasts toward recent 7–14 day moving average.
- Lagged response to sentiment shifts: if sentiment drops sharply, model doesn’t adjust forecast within 3–5 days — introduce a 2–3 day smoothing delay for sentiment-driven corrections.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day horizon: model tends to overfit short-term momentum, especially when sentiment is volatile — reduce forecast variance in high-sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.00 for 3+ days), reduce forecast slope and bias toward historical mean — avoid “false recovery” signals.
